label: Catastrophic risk: the future a catastrophe could cost

rows.label: World population in the long run (people alive in a typical future year)

source.title: United Nations, Global Issues: Population (World Population Prospects 2024)
source.quote: After reaching this peak, it is expected to gradually decline to around 10.2 billion by the century's end.

rows.explainer: People alive in each future year, the yearly stream of healthy life a catastrophe that shrinks or ends humanity's future would cost: the UN's 2100 projection as the best guess (after its peak of about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s). The range is ours: a lower population if decline continues past 2100, a higher one if it doesn't. Every model's future loss is this stream discounted at the shared rate (your discount rate is how much future generations count).
